packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-04 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

EXPOSURE STATEMENT
No proposed identification or earlier reading of this item was present in my
context. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..009 in this packet; no packet.json,
no web, no search. Nothing beyond the rules.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

Two overviews, each a tall narrow crop of a book gutter:

image-001 (tiles 002-005): upright. Three zones, left to right:
  (i)  a sliver of a leaf at far left carrying a small cursive hand in brown ink
       (only a few letters per line, about 35 lines); a short addition in darker
       ink about two thirds down. Not covered by any tile on this face.
  (ii) in the gutter, a vertical run of several narrow parchment pieces (at
       least five, overlapping like guards/reinforcing strips) with faint pale
       brown marks in horizontal rows. Some rows have ruled lines. The marks look
       like script but are very pale; they may be offset, washed or reversed
       writing rather than direct ink. Tentative only.
  (iii) at right, the left edge of a written column in a formal book hand, black
       ink, ruled in ink, with a large red initial B (about 3 lines) at the top,
       a red initial A (2 lines, with a long red descending flourish) lower down,
       and red strokes touching several capitals (S of "Seneca", A of "Aug",
       H of "Hec"). Only the first 5-9 letters of each line are in the crop.
       The column ends about two thirds down; blank ruled margin below.
  No running title, no marginal or interlinear gloss visible in this crop. The
  crop is too tight to tell how many columns the page has.

image-006 (tiles 007-009): upright; apparently the same gutter from the other
  side of the opening. Left: line-ENDS of the brown cursive hand (same kind of
  hand as zone (i)), with a darker-ink insertion beside two lines. Centre: the
  parchment strips, here blank (only speckled hair-side texture and smudges;
  no script found). Right: a blank, stained parchment surface with faint ruling.

Which element is "the fragment" is not stated; I report all three.

2. SPANS SELECTED
- Zone (iii), book-hand column: all 35 line-openings read (tiles 002-005).
- Cursive line-ends on image-006: read from tiles 007-009 as far as possible.
- Cursive sliver on image-001: overview only (reduced), read tentatively.
- Strips: examined in every tile; no secure reading (see section 3c).
Unread: everything to the right of the crop in zone (iii) and everything to the
left of the crops in the cursive text. A wider view of both pages is needed for
any connected prose; none can be had from these crops.

Conventions: abbreviation marks kept where typeable; proposed expansions in
parentheses; "?" after uncertain readings; "..." = text continues beyond the
crop. Line numbers count from the top of the named tile; tiles overlap, and the
overlaps are noted, not counted twice.

3. TRANSCRIPTION

(a) Zone (iii): left edge of the book-hand column

image-002 l.1   [red initial B, three lines high] E? ...
image-002 l.2   [beside initial] c? ...
image-002 l.3   [beside initial] o? ...
image-002 l.4   repleta. ? ...
image-002 l.5   ee (esse) q(uod) nul ...
image-002 l.6   Seneca. ? ...      (S touched red; a red-touched letter follows)
image-002 l.7   q(uod) nõ (non) e(st) d ...
image-002 l.8   bono i(n)g(ra)? ...   (written "bono ĩgm"/"ĩgra", cut)
image-002 l.9   tac(i)o(n)e cu(m)? ...   (possibly the end of a word divided from l.8)
image-002 l.10  bon(us)?. Aug ...   (A touched red; "Aug" with suspension)
image-002 l.11  [tops only; = image-003 l.3]

image-003 l.1-2 = image-002 l.9-10 (overlap)
image-003 l.3   ⁊ (et) illic ma ...
image-003 l.4   unt ut ? ...
image-003 l.5   [red initial A, two lines] vdi ...
image-003 l.6   [beside initial] cas? il ...
image-003 l.7   a deo. Et ...
image-003 l.8   c(um)? v(er)ba de ...
image-003 l.9   .i. (id est) simul ...
image-003 l.10  meditãdo (meditando) ...
image-003 l.11  de ip(s)is ul ...
image-003 l.12  dormiẽdo. (dormiendo) ...
image-003 l.13  oc(u)los pon ...
image-003 l.14  ut e(st)? pug? ...    ("ut" + a barred letter + "puge"/"pugc")
image-003 l.15  [tops only; = image-004 l.4]

image-004 l.1-3 = image-003 l.12-14 (overlap)
image-004 l.4   Hec s(un)t? de ...      (H touched red)
image-004 l.5   s(un)t v(er)ba q(ue)? di ...
image-004 l.6   corã (coram). i. me ...
image-004 l.7   d(omin)o? de(us)? t. q(u)i ...   (three short abbreviated words with
                superscript signs; expansions very uncertain)
image-004 l.8   p(ri)mas man ...
image-004 l.9   ho(m)i(n)? usq(ue) g ...
image-004 l.10  s(upe)rflue. n(on)? ...
image-004 l.11  ih(es)u d(omi)ne g ...
image-004 l.12  ul' (vel) senatũ? ...     (or "seriatũ"; second word uncertain)
image-004 l.13  la?. n(on)? iumen ...
image-004 l.14  q(u)i app? ul' (vel) e ...
image-004 l.15  lanis?. ille ...          (first word uncertain: "lanis"/"lauis")
image-004 l.16  capite mo ...

image-005 l.1-3 = image-004 l.14-16 (overlap)
image-005 l.4   me corona ...
image-005 l.5   meo p(ro) ope ...
image-005 l.6   ul' (vel) s(an)c(t)i? iniqu? ...
[column ends; blank ruled space below]

Observation: "Seneca." and "Aug" with red-touched capitals look like named
authorities opening citations; ".i." (id est) occurs at least twice. Tentative
interpretation only: prose with cited authorities and glossing "id est" phrases.
I do not infer the work.

(b) Brown cursive hand, line-ends on image-006 (left zone)

Only the last 2-8 letters of each line are in the crop. Readings are tentative
throughout.

image-007 (top tile): line-ends, top to bottom:
  ...is / ...s [de?] / ...tri / ...? / ...m / ...? / ...o? / ...m.
  (eight ends; none gives a whole word)

image-008 (middle tile; its first lines overlap the last of image-007):
  l.1  ...m
  l.2  ...?
  l.3  ...o?
  l.4  ...m.      (a superscript o above)
  l.5  ...d(omi)ne?   ("dne" with mark)
  l.6  ...t
  l.7  ...n
  l.8  ...a n(ost)ra?   ("a nr̃a")
  l.9  ...⁊ (et)
  l.10 ...u?
  l.11 ...bis,   + darker-ink addition beginning "dor?" (cut by the strip)
  l.12 ...emis?.  + darker-ink addition beginning "C?" (cut by the strip)
  l.13 ...volem(us)?    (or "volam(us)")
  l.14 ...ntig(us)?
  l.15 ...ete?
  l.16 ...tte?
  l.17 ...s g(e)nte?    ("g̃nte")
  l.18 ...trium?        ("triu" with mark)
  l.19 ...ijs alis?

image-009 (bottom tile; first four lines repeat image-008 l.16-19):
  l.5  ... q(uod) adl? ...
  l.6  ...gillie?
  l.7  ...n(ost)ri? ang[...]
  l.8  ...? v(er)o? sic
  l.9  ...lhe? videt(ur)?
  l.10 ...vocat?      (small, perhaps interlinear or a short line)
  l.11 ...i, vni(us)?
  l.12 ...tatco?      (a heavier, boxed or underlined word; unread)
  l.13 ...co ope.     (heavier ink)
  l.14 ...Mag?        (last visible line, faint)

The darker additions at image-008 l.11-12 are in a different, blacker ink and a
smaller cursive; they sit to the right of the line-ends and are cut off by the
strip. Observation: a later marginal or interlinear addition. Not expanded.

(c) Brown cursive sliver on image-001 (zone (i), overview only)

About 35 line fragments of 3-7 letters each at reduced size. Possible letter
groups, all uncertain: "...le cur", "...lutis", "...glosam?", "...bis, dor"
with the same darker addition (so this is the same page as (b), seen with more
of the line-ends covered or uncovered by the strip), "...volam?", "...thebet?",
"...q' aute?", "...h(ab)ijs alis", "...videt". I do not offer these as readings
for matching; a native-resolution tile of this zone is needed.

(d) Parchment strips in the gutter

image-001 side (tiles 002-005): pale brown marks in rows, some rows on ruled
lines. I looked at each piece in each tile. Letter-like shapes are present
(loops, minims, an "a"-like form, a group resembling "goia" at the foot of
image-002, groups resembling "ihs", "lan", "enb", "ran" on image-003, and a
ruled piece with minim groups on image-004), but no group could be read as a
word in either normal or mirrored direction, and I cannot tell whether the marks
are the strips' own faded script, offset from the facing page, or show-through.
[illegible] for the strips as a whole; this reflects the pallor of the marks at
this resolution, not a lack of inspection.

image-006 side (tiles 007-009): the strips show no script, only speckling,
creases and a dark smudge about a third of the way down.

4. LIMITATIONS
- Every text in this packet is cut by the crop: zone (iii) gives only line
  openings; the cursive text gives only line-ends. No connected clause can be
  transcribed, so a later source match will have to rest on sequences of
  line-openings (e.g. "repleta. / esse quod nul... / Seneca. ... / quod non est
  d... / bono ... / ...tacione cum / bon. Aug..." and "...a deo. Et / ... verba
  de / .i. simul / meditando / de ipsis ul... / dormiendo. / oculos pon...").
- Many abbreviations are resolved only tentatively; superscript signs in
  image-004 l.7-11 are especially insecure.
- Needed: a full-width view of the column at right of image-001; a full view of
  the cursive page; and raking-light or enhanced (UV / contrast-stretched)
  images of the strips, including a mirrored view to test for offset.
- This is an unverified image reading.
